evidence.title: Lyft to pay $272 million settlement to California drivers

occurrences.checkable_against: California-Lyft settlement agreement and court docket
occurrences.quote_span: A settlement has finally been reached in the six-year lawsuit California waged against the rideshare giant Lyft. The company will pay $272.5 million to settle claims that it committed wage theft against its drivers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: California-Lyft settlement agreement and third-party fund administration documents
occurrences.quote_span: Lyft has agreed to pay a $272.5 million settlement; the majority of that money, around $237 million, will be placed in a third-party fund to be administered to drivers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Lyft 2025 Economic Impact Report for Los Angeles
occurrences.quote_span: In 2025, 80% of L.A. Lyft drivers were members of a community of color and more than two-thirds of its drivers spoke Spanish at home.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Lyft financial reports for the years targeted by the lawsuit
occurrences.quote_span: During the years targeted in the lawsuit, Lyft reported a total revenue of $9.5 billion.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Court docket and settlement approval order
occurrences.quote_span: The settlement must still be approved by the court.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Lyft yearly Economic Impact Reports
occurrences.quote_span: Data from Lyft’s yearly Economic Impact Reports show that immigrants and communities of color carry the bulk of driver demographics year after year.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: California Attorney General and city attorneys' 2020 lawsuit filing against Lyft
occurrences.quote_span: California Attorney General Rob Bonta, alongside the city attorneys of Los Angeles, San Diego and San Francisco, sued Lyft in 2020 after the company was accused of misclassifying drivers as independent contractors from 2016 through 2020.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: California lawsuit complaint and applicable California wage-and-hour records
occurrences.quote_span: This misclassification meant drivers were paid well below minimum wage and were denied other legally required workplace protections.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement by Los Angeles City Attorney Hydee Feldstein Soto
occurrences.quote_span: “This historic settlement sends a clear message: companies must follow the law, pay their fair share and play by the rules.”
occurrences.speaker: Hydee Feldstein Soto
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Third-party settlement administrator notices and claims process documents
occurrences.quote_span: Once the court approves the settlement and payments start being made, eligible drivers will be notified through the third-party administrator when it is time for them to submit their information for restitution.
occurrences.speaker: California Attorney General's office
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Lyft 2025 Economic Impact Report for Los Angeles
occurrences.quote_span: Nearly half of all the Lyft drivers in L.A. last year (47%) were Latino.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement by Los Angeles City Attorney Hydee Feldstein Soto
occurrences.quote_span: “When companies misclassify their workers, they deny them critical protections and shift the burden onto taxpayers,” Los Angeles City Attorney Hydee Feldstein Soto said in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Hydee Feldstein Soto
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement by California Attorney General Rob Bonta
occurrences.quote_span: “Lyft’s success would not be possible without the drivers Lyft sought to unfairly short-change. Hard-working employees deserve full compensation for their labor.”
occurrences.speaker: Rob Bonta
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Statement by California Attorney General Rob Bonta
occurrences.quote_span: “Rideshare companies like Lyft have enjoyed massive growth and profits on the backs of drivers over the past decade, many of whom are from immigrant communities and communities of color,” Bonta said in a statement.
occurrences.speaker: Rob Bonta
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: California-Lyft settlement agreement and claims administrator eligibility formula
occurrences.quote_span: The eligibility and compensation for drivers will be determined based on the hours and total miles driven between April 2016 and December 2020.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: ShiftTracker driver earnings dataset
occurrences.quote_span: The average Lyft driver makes anywhere between $11 and $18 an hour after factoring in expenses, according to data compiled by ShiftTracker.
occurrences.speaker: ShiftTracker
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement

occurrences.checkable_against: Lyft settlement statement or court settlement agreement
occurrences.quote_span: Although Lyft has agreed to pay the settlement to end litigation, the company still denies any wrongdoing.
occurrences.speaker: Lyft
occurrences.subject: Lyft California driver wage-theft settlement
